flashcards.q: What is the correct time allocation inside a single STAR answer?
flashcards.a: S 10% (~15s), T 10% (~15s), A 50% (~90s), R 15% (~25s), rejected alternative 10% (~20s), what I'd change 5% (~10s). Candidates invert this by spending 60% on Situation.

flashcards.q: What two parts of a STAR answer separate senior from staff, and are usually omitted?
flashcards.a: The alternative you rejected (and the cost you accepted), and what you would do differently now. Without the first you read as 'found one thing that worked' rather than 'chose'; without the second you read as not learning.

flashcards.q: What distinguishes an assigned story from a claimed story, and why does it matter?
flashcards.a: 'My manager asked me to migrate the batch job' is senior. 'I noticed it was the only JVM service in a Python fleet, costing a second build pipeline and on-call runbook, so I proposed and ran the migration' is staff. Same project, different level. Lead with claimed stories.

flashcards.q: How long should the 60-second version of a story be, structurally?
flashcards.a: Nine sentences: one Situation, one Task, three Action, one Result, one rejected alternative. Then stop and offer a direction. Never give the 3-minute version unprompted.

flashcards.q: Which resume numbers must never be rounded, and why?
flashcards.a: 54,486 skills; 3,447 Java lines removed; 812-line Python service; 307 commits; 178K+ net LOC; 1.2M+ skill rows; 2,000+ golden baseline rows; 22 locales. Odd numbers are credible precisely because they are odd. 'About fifty thousand' destroys the signal.

flashcards.q: What is the weakest link in this resume's story set, and what must be prepared first?
flashcards.a: The ~25% engagement uplift. A metric with no stated measurement method is the single most likely place a Bar Raiser breaks the story. Define the metric, the comparison design (holdout vs pre/post), the window, and the tenant scope before any other prep.

flashcards.q: OOM story: what was the symptom, why was raising the memory limit wrong, and why is gc.collect() a smell?
flashcards.a: Symptom: process killed with no Python traceback (kernel OOM killer, not an exception). Raising the limit was wrong because peak memory scaled with corpus size not batch size, so the failure returns at the next growth step. gc.collect() compensates for CPython allocator behaviour; the structural fix is streaming with generators and bounded batches.

flashcards.q: Why was patching only the endpoints you found the wrong fix for the cross-tenant authorization bypass?
flashcards.a: The class of bug is 'authorization decided per endpoint'. Fixing instances leaves the class. Enforcement belongs on the object-fetch path keyed on the authenticated tenant. Middleware is insufficient because it sees the route and token but not which object IDs the handler is about to load.

flashcards.q: Why is 812 lines of Python a faithful replacement for 3,447 lines of Java, not a feature cut?
flashcards.a: Most of the Java was Spring Batch scaffolding: item readers, writers, processors, job and step configuration. The actual transformation rules were a small fraction. Lead with that when someone assumes functionality was dropped.

flashcards.q: Why choose a contextual bandit over a supervised ranker for recommendations?
flashcards.a: A supervised ranker trained on logged clicks learns the previous policy's preferences, so new content is never shown and therefore never generates data justifying showing it. Offline replay flatters supervised models because it scores against the logged policy. The missing piece was off-policy evaluation via inverse propensity scoring.

flashcards.q: What is the honest framing of the vLLM self-hosting decision?
flashcards.a: Not 'self-host everything' but 'split by workload shape': self-hosted vLLM on SageMaker for the high-volume online path, Bedrock batch for offline generation, hosted frontier API for tasks needing frontier quality. The stated gap: no dollar break-even model was built.

flashcards.q: MongoDB race conditions and event loop errors: what were the causes and the wrong fixes?
flashcards.a: Race: read-modify-write across a network round trip is not atomic. Wrong fix was app-level locking (serialises a hot path). Right fix: atomic update operator with a filter condition, so concurrency control lives with the data. Loop errors: a client created on one event loop used from another, or a module-level client outliving its loop. Wrong fix: broad try/except. Right fix: loop-scoped client lifecycle bound to startup/shutdown.

flashcards.q: Why was the ETL story sold on cycle time rather than runtime?
flashcards.a: 4.5 hours means one marketing optimisation cycle per working day, so the runtime was the constraint on the business process. '9x faster pipeline' is an engineering fact; 'marketing can optimise several times a day instead of once' is why it got funded.

flashcards.q: Which stories must exist before entering any senior loop?
flashcards.a: Disagreed AND was wrong. A real failure with a real COST. Said no and lost. Influenced without authority. Reframed a wrong requirement. Prevented an expensive mistake. Missing any of these leaves a rubric column empty.

flashcards.q: What does the write-up 'could not determine candidate's personal contribution' mean, and what causes it?
flashcards.a: It is the most common cause of a no-hire on an otherwise strong story, and the cause is 'we' throughout the Action section. Fix: first person singular in every Action sentence. 'I decided', 'I benchmarked', 'I rejected'.

flashcards.q: Why do golden-baseline assertions have to be on aggregate behaviour rather than exact string equality?
flashcards.a: A semantic system whose output must be byte-identical cannot be improved. The design decision is separating 'must never change' (locale precedence, tenant scoping, pagination: exact assertions) from 'may drift within tolerance' (rankings, resolutions: aggregate assertions with tolerance bands).

flashcards.q: What is the coverage rule for a story-to-competency matrix?
flashcards.a: No competency column may be empty, and no single story may be the lead for more than about three competencies. Interviewers share written notes, so telling one story all loop is visible in the packet.

flashcards.q: What resume defect must be fixed before an AWS-literate interviewer reads it?
flashcards.a: ml.4xlarge and g4.2xlarge are not valid SageMaker instance identifiers. The real ones are almost certainly ml.g4dn.2xlarge and ml.g5.xlarge. It is a ten-second credibility loss on the strongest technical story.
